sentences.text: Nurhachius was a pterosaur with an estimated wingspan between 2.4 and 2.5 meters, though a 2008 estimate placed the span at 228 centimeters and the weight at 4 kilograms.
Its skull featured a large nasoantorbital fenestra, an opening that occupied 58 percent of the skull length, while the lower jaws measured 290 millimeters in length.
The animal possessed 54 teeth in total, with 28 in the upper jaw and 26 in the lower jaw; these teeth were robust, curved backward, and had three roots, limited to the front of the jaws.
The skull contained a massive opening called the nasoantorbital fenestra, which took up more than half of the entire skull length.
Researchers noted a unique warped deltopectoral crest on the humerus, a structure shared with the Istiodactylus and Anhangueridae clades.

The genus was named in 2005 by Wang Xiaolin, Alexander Kellner, Zhou Zhonghe, and Diogenes de Almeida Campos, honoring Nurhaci, the first emperor of the Qing Dynasty, and Ignácio Aureliano Machado Brito, a Brazilian paleontologist.
The original description relied on specimen IVPP V-13288, a partial skull and skeleton, and a second species, Nurhachius luei, was named in 2019.
Cladistic analysis by Wang and colleagues placed Nurhachius within the family Istiodactylidae, a relationship supported by a 2008 analysis by Lü Junchang.
Zhou and colleagues confirmed the membership of Nurhachius in the family Istiodactylidae in 2019.
Nurhachius lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago, in the Jiufotang Formation of Chaoyang, Liaoning, China.
In 2008, Lü suggested that Nurhachius might be a junior synonym of Liaoxipterus.
A 2024 analysis by Hone et al. recovered the genus as paraphyletic, with N. luei being closer to Hongshanopterus.
